newsitem.title: USA: Seagram slumps after analysts' meeting.
newsitem.headline: Seagram slumps after analysts' meeting.

text.p: Shares of Canadian beverage and entertainment company Seagram Co Ltd fell on Wednesday on investor concerns about the company's strategy to focus more of its capital on its entertainment business.

"There's a lot of concern about how they are going to use their capital," said PaineWebber Inc analyst Christopher Dixon. "Basically, what they went out yesterday and said was they plan to use their capital to build up and invest in the entertainment business and they would not be spending that time and energy investing in the beverages."
Seagram outlined its plans Tuesday in New York.
Shares of Seagram were down 1-1/2 or nearly four percent to 36-1/2 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Dixon said the drop is not surprising because many of the beverage analysts who follow the company are not sure the strategy of using the free cash generated from the spirits division to finance the entertainment division will pay off.

Dixon said the move should improve Seagram's return on capital but it will take time for Seagram's MCA Inc to achieve its goals. Seagram acquired an 80 percent stake in MCA in June 1995 for $5.7 billion in an effort to diversify beyond its core beverage operations.
Dean Witter Reynolds analyst Alan Kassan, who cut his rating on Seagram to neutral from accumulate based on price, said investors are concerned about Seagram's strategy.

"The economics of the film business are still unfavorable and (MCA's) output agreements with some of the European broadcasters don't fully kick in until three to five years out, so until that point it's going to be a hit or miss business."
MCA have said their goal is to increase profitability at the studio and become one of the leading providers of music, film, theme parks and television programming.

However, such moves are likely to result in significant expenditures, particularly on the theme park business where MCA is planning to spend more than $1 billion to develop a new theme park in Osaka, Japan and a second theme park in Orlando, Florida.
